messages:
olivia-customer: Hey team, our rerank responses suddenly started returning weird negative and non-normalized scores today. Example response attached below, customer is confused and threatening to revert. Can someone help?

olivia-customer: curl example we sent:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "best backup solution for postgres", "candidates": ["use pg_dump","streaming wal","logical replication","snapshot-based backup"]}'
```

olivia-customer: sample returned scores (order preserved): [ -3.42, 0.12, -0.98, -1.75 ]

emma-cs: thanks for the repro — sorry about the churn :confused:  Quick questions: which SDK/version are you on, and are you batching multiple queries in the same request? Also can you paste the raw request_id from the headers (the x-rw-request-id) so we can lookup logs?

olivia-customer: SDK v0.9.2 (python). Not batching, one query per request. request_id: rw-2025-07-15-9b2f

harry-ml: short answer: those are expected shape-wise — rerank returns raw model scores (logits) by default which are unbounded and can be negative. They aren't probabilities unless you apply a softmax per-query. Negative values alone don't mean wrong. That said, the customer expects normalized probabilities.

harry-ml: quick guidance to convert to probabilities client-side:```python
import math
scores = [-3.42, 0.12, -0.98, -1.75]
max_s = max(scores)
exp = [math.exp(s - max_s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
print(probs)
```

liam-eng: adding infra/ops note: i pulled the request logs for rw-2025-07-15-9b2f — model served was rerank-v2-2025-06, no throttles or partial failures. Latency looks normal (~120ms). No sign of a server-side normalization flag being set.

olivia-customer: Got it. Our product team insists the API used to return probabilities (0-1 normalized) last quarter though. Could that have changed? Clients downstream already expect sums to ~1.

emma-cs: possibility: older SDK had a wrapper that applied softmax before returning results. Newer SDKs return raw scores and defer interpretation. Which UI/SDK version did you upgrade between? The v0.9.x release notes mention changing rerank return semantics to raw scores to standardize across languages.

olivia-customer: hmm we did upgrade from 0.8.7 to 0.9.2 last month across most services. We missed one microservice though — could that cause mixed behavior?

harry-ml: mixing versions can definitely cause confusion: old clients would see normalized outputs, new ones raw logits. Two immediate options: 1) we can enable a compatibility shim on our gateway to return normalized probabilities for your org (short-term) — needs ops approval, or 2) you can compute softmax client-side (recommended long-term).

liam-eng: ops note: enabling shim (normalize=true) for a single org is doable, but we need an RFC and a short config window. I'll open a ticket if you want us to proceed.

olivia-customer: please open the ticket, product team is pushing for minimal change on their side. ETA tight.

emma-cs: putting this on our priority queue. For immediate unblock — harry, can you paste a one-liner curl that returns normalized scores via inference helper so we can share with the customer?

harry-ml: sure:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank?normalize=true \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"best backup solution for postgres","candidates":["use pg_dump","streaming wal","logical replication","snapshot-based backup"]}' | jq .scores
```

harry-ml: Note: normalize=true triggers a post-processing softmax on the scores in the gateway. It's not available in all older SDKs. If you want fully deterministic probabilities across runs, you should softmax per-query client-side with a stable implementation (subtracting max before exp).

olivia-customer: ok this helps a lot — thanks. Can you also confirm billing implications? Do normalized scores change token counts or any billing metrics?

liam-eng: no billing change — normalization is just a numeric post-process on the scores, no extra tokens. If we enable shim it won't affect usage logging.

emma-cs: next steps: 1) liam open ops ticket to enable normalize=true for org: acme-corp 2) customer to roll back any places that assumed logits vs probs, or switch to client softmax 3) we'll follow up with release notes pointer so you can pin SDK versions.

olivia-customer: thanks team, appreciate the quick triage. Please CC me on the ops ticket and I'll update product. :pray:

support-bot: Ticket created: OPS-5421 (enable-rerank-normalize-for-acme-corp) — assignee: liam-eng, priority: high.
